description: Implements FORMULATION.md section 2 (Boxleiter method, three-bucket scheme, low/mid/high band).
signature: def estimate_sales(review_count: pd.Series, genre_bucket: pd.Series, params: EnrichmentParams) -> pd.DataFrame
docstring:
Compute estimated sales bands.

Args:
    review_count: r_i per appid.
    genre_bucket: map_genre_bucket's output per appid.
    params: EnrichmentParams.boxleiter_multipliers.

Returns:
    A DataFrame with columns estimated_sales_low, estimated_sales_mid, estimated_sales_high, computed as review_count * m_low/mid/high(genre_bucket) respectively.
preconditions: review_count >= 0 for every row (0 is valid, e.g. a brand-new candidate with no reviews yet)
Every genre_bucket value has a corresponding entry in params.boxleiter_multipliers
postconditions: estimated_sales_low <= estimated_sales_mid <= estimated_sales_high for every row, per the module's own invariant (guaranteed structurally since the multiplier triple itself is validated ordered by config.validate_parameters)
review_count == 0 produces estimated_sales_low == mid == high == 0, per the module's edge case, not NaN

edge_cases.expected_behavior: all three sales columns are exactly 0.0, row is kept (still informs competition density downstream)

edge_cases.input: genre_bucket value not present in params.boxleiter_multipliers (should not happen if map_genre_bucket only ever returns the three known keys)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: raises EnrichmentError -- treated as a programmer-error / config-drift condition, not a normal data edge case

edge_cases.input: review_count is very large (a breakout hit with hundreds of thousands of reviews)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: no ceiling applied here; the coarse filter's own 'no review-count ceiling' decision means this function must not silently cap the multiplication either

unit_tests.name: test_reproduces_hand_computed_values
unit_tests.description: review_count=1000, bucket='mainstream' with multipliers (30,37,45) yields (30000, 37000, 45000), per the module's own testing requirement.

unit_tests.name: test_ordering_low_mid_high_holds
unit_tests.description: For a batch of synthetic rows across all three buckets, low <= mid <= high always holds.
unit_tests.expected: monotonic ordering holds for every row

unit_tests.name: test_unknown_bucket_raises
unit_tests.description: A genre_bucket value not in boxleiter_multipliers raises EnrichmentError.
